steps.title: Confirm metabolic acidosis
steps.body: Low pH with low bicarbonate. Calculate anion gap: Na − (Cl + HCO3). Normal gap ~8–12 mEq/L.
steps.tip: Always correct for albumin: AG + 2.5 × (4 − albumin).

steps.title: High anion gap?
steps.body: If AG is elevated, think MUDPILES: Methanol, Uremia, DKA, Propylene glycol, Isoniazid/Iron, Lactic acidosis, Ethylene glycol, Salicylates.
steps.tip: Osmolar gap helps detect toxic alcohols.

steps.title: Check for concurrent disorders
steps.body: Use Winter's formula: expected PCO2 = (1.5 × HCO3) + 8 ± 2. Higher measured PCO2 suggests superimposed respiratory acidosis.
steps.tip: Delta-delta analysis detects mixed acid-base disorders.

steps.title: Normal anion gap acidosis
steps.body: If gap is normal, think GI bicarbonate loss, RTA type 1/2/4, or saline infusion. Urine anion gap helps distinguish RTA vs diarrhea.
steps.tip: Urine AG negative in diarrhea; positive in RTA.

steps.title: Treat the underlying cause
steps.body: DKA → insulin and fluids. Lactic acidosis → perfusion. Toxins → antidote and dialysis. Severe acidemia pH <7.1 may need bicarbonate cautiously.
steps.tip: Bicarbonate is controversial in DKA once insulin started.
